summary: No separate Detransitive sense list is printed: sense 1 in Detransitive examples denotes the existing digging/hewing meaning with a patient perspective. Do not invent another lexical meaning. The inherited Infinitiv filing is retained; ḥforo itself does not assert a patient perspective.

Lahdo komәḥforo supports a Detransitive Infectum box, but the installation description does not decide ongoing process versus a resulting state. Part. Pass. explicitly describes excavated rock, openings and graves.

Preterit admits l-marked lexical agents (PrS 16/62, 17/9), whereas extra l-suffixes can index an affected beneficiary/victim beside a bare pit object (JTM 5.2/39, 29/271). Do not equate all l-marking.

Infectum-wa describes repeated craft/agricultural procedures; Infinitiv occurs with ability, purpose and tools. Surface variants include assimilated ḥfəlle/ḥfəlli, retained r in ḥfiroli and contracted ḥofanno. The supplied Ḥufríwayle at old houses/37 differs in Unicode accent composition from verse Ḥufríwayle; do not silently replace either.

Compact routine records lack independent verse evidence and are retained provisionally. Existing examples at 75/294, 116/31, LB 76, 77/85, 81/2 and 93/12 are not duplicated. The hewn-rock use is already covered by aushauen.
The new idiom is coordinated full verbs, not a light verb plus noun. Ordinary digging a grave remains literal elsewhere.

All 19 occurrences checked. Round 1 already fills Preterit, Infectum, Infectum-wa and Detransitive Part. Pass. cells; Jan routine tokens are not added merely because the reader counted only the original entry.

Retained-r ḥfər- variants contrast with inherited assimilated ḥfəlle. ḥfərwole supplies Preterit-wa; ḥfərlele has agent and possible beneficiary suffixes. The grammatical identity of every -le is not assumed.
Inherited Detransitive Infinitiv filing is preserved, though ḥforo plus an active cognate finite verb has no Detransitive meaning.

summary: Instrument subject: the plough point digs the soil. Excavated material (aggregate), worked ground (stony plots), house/site and grave remain ordinary digging/hewing objects.
Printing moulds/blocks extend aushauen technically; cognate ḥforo ḥfərənne adds a construction, not a new meaning. Cisterns, kilns and trenches remain ordinary excavation.
